Jayaprakash M vs Punitha on 4 October, 2025
Kabc020067232024
 In The Court Of Xxi Addl.Small Cause Judge And
 Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore.

(Scch-23)
 Dated This The 4th Day Of October - 2025

Present: Sri. Shreyansh Doddamani
 B.Com. Ll.B, (Spl)
 Xxi Addl.

SCJ & ACJM  MEMBER - MACT, BENGALURU.
 MVC. No.1144/2024

Petitioner : Sri. M. Jayaprakash,
 S/o Munichowdappa,
 Aged about 43 years,
 R/at No..., Main road,
 Doddavallabi,
 Kolar-563133.

(By Sri.M.V. Vishwanath, Advocate)
 v/s Respondent/s : 1. Mrs. Punitha,
 W/o Arun,
 R/at : No.58/1, Mysore Road,
 Near Maramma Temple Road,
 Bengaluru-560039  RC owner of motorcycle bearing  Reg.No.KA-41-EW-9439)
 (Exparte)
 SCCH-23 2 MVC No.1144/2024  2.

The Legal Manager,
 Magma HDI Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd.,
 No.36, HM Astrid, 1st Floor,
 Minerva Circle,
 Bengaluru-560052.
 (Insurer of motorcycle bearing  Reg.No.KA-41-EW-9439)
 Policy No.P0024300004/4113/106538  valid from 16.09.2023 to 15.09.2028

(By Sri.M.E. Madhu Sudhan, Adv)
 JUDGMENT Jayaprakash M vs Punitha on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69775080/
1
This claim petition is filed u/s 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a RTA.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that on 21.01.2024 at about 11.30 p.m, as the petitioner was carefully standing on the side of the road, near Little Flower School to HP Petrol Bunk, Dr. Punith Rajkumar Main road, BSK 3 rd Stage, Bengaluru City, at that time the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.NoKA-41-EW-9439 came at high speed in rash and negligent manner so as to endangering to human life and dashed to the petitioner.

Due to tremendous impact petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries & immediately shifted to Vinayaka Hospital, and after first aid he was shifted to Rashtrootthana Hospital, RR Nagar, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and underwent several surgeries.
He has spent substantial amount towards medical and other incidental expenses.
He stated that due to the accidental injuries he lost income from the date of accident and he fully disabled to avocation and loss earning capacity.
Looking to the nature of injuries he permanently disabled.

The accident was caused due to rash and negligence rider of the motorcycle,
the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the vehicle are jointly & severally liable to pay compensation.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence she was placed exparte.
4. The respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement denied the issuance insurance policy in respect of motorcycle in favour of respondent No.1.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.

Further this respondent denied the negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle and contended that the accident took place due to the negligence of petitioner himself who was crossing the road where there was no zebra crossing or provision for crossing the road.
Further the respondent has contended that, the owner and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provision of Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the rider of the offending vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 21.01.2024 at about 11.30 p.m, when he was carefully standing on the side of the road near Little Flower School to HP Petrol Bunk, Dr. Punith Rajkumar Main road, BSK 3rd Stage, Bengaluru City, at that time the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-EW-9439 drove the same at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against him.
As a result of forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries ?

Jayaprakash M vs Punitha on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69775080/
2 2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
6.
The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 16 were marked on his behalf.
The petitioner has examined the MRO as PW.2, through him got marked Ex.P.17 to 20 documents.
Further Dr.Ramesh. B was examined as PW.3 and got marked Ex.P.21 & 22 documents.
In order to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 Ins.Co.Ltd, got examined its official as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 & 2 documents.
7. Heard counsel for the petitioner on merits.
In spite sufficient opportunity has been given, the respondent No.2 has not adduced his arguments.
However, in spite of liberty has been granted to file written arguments before two days from the date of pronouncement of judgment, they have not filed any written arguments.
Hence arguments of respondents side taken as nil.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

8. My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1 :
The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.20 lakhs together.

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by son of petitioner, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the rider of the motorcycle for the offences punishable under section's 279, 338 of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
10. Though the respondent No.2 insurance company denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence.
No doubt, the official of the said company was examined as RW.1 but his evidence is no way helpful to prove the defence of respondent No.2.
Because he is not an eye-witness to the accident and his evidence is not supported by any document.

During the course of his cross examination RW.1 stated that according to the FIR and the charge sheet, it is correct that the accident occurred when the applicant was standing on the side of the road.
The witness continues and says that he has misrepresented it.
No independent witness was either produced by the insurer of the vehicle to displace the version of the accident as deposed by PW.1 in this case.
Hence the respondents No.2 utterly failed to discharge the burden that was placed on them.
Added to this the respondent No.2 did not make any attempt to examine the rider of its insured vehicle who is the best witness to depose about the cause of accident.
There is no explanation to that effect.
Non-examination of the said rider is fatal to the defence of respondent No.2.

Hence its contention that there was no negligence on the part of motorcycle has to be Jayaprakash M vs Punitha on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69775080/
3 disbelieved.
With this observation, I hold that the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of offending motorcycle is proved.
In this view of the matter no iota of negligence can be attributed on the part of the petitioner in the occurrence of resultant accident.

With this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
11. ISSUE NO.2 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the vehicle.
Therefore he is entitled for compensation.
12. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME :
The petitioner has produced his Aadhaar card which is marked as Ex.P.16, as per the above said document wherein his date of birth is reflected as 06.06.1980.
This indicates that he was aged (43 years 7 months 15 days) 44 years on the date of accident.
13. The petitioner deposed that prior to the accident he was working as driver and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
No documents have been produced to establish the avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in his evidence affidavit.
It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA. No.101144/2020 (MV) dated. 05.07.2023.

Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the year 2024.
Therefore, Rs.16,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.
14. As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : 1) Right tibia-Segmental- comminuted fracture (2) Right calf abrasion.
It is needless to say that the injury No.1 is grievous and injury No.2 is simple in nature.

He has produced Ex.P12 Discharge summaries (2 in no's), discloses that he has taken treatment as an inpatient for the period from 22.01.2024 to 29.01.2024 (8 days) and from 19.02.2024 to 26.02.2024 (8 days).
In total he took treatment for a period of 16 days.

As per discharge summary during the course of treatment he had undergone surgeries in the form of :
Jayaprakash M vs Punitha on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69775080/
4 1) Fasciotomy + Debridement, 2) Suprapatella Nailing + Split skin grafting 3)
Arthroscopic ACL and PCL reconstruction and MCL.
15.
It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has thereby lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined Dr.Ramesh. B as PW.3 who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has sustained total permanent physical disability of 30% of right lower limb and 15% disability to the whole body.
It is elicited during the course of cross examination PW.3 categorically admitted that he has not treated the petitioner and he has also not seen the medical records.
He admitted that the fractures are united and he underwent surgery to the Tibia and fibula is normal.
He stated that the petitioner can do his profession with some difficulty.
He admitted that the applicant's surgery and treatment were successful.
However from the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.3 has assessed the disability on the higher side.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor,
the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 10%, cannot be ruled out.

Therefore, I consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 10%.
16. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES : The period of hospitalization of 16 days is proved with a help of discharge summary.

During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet,
transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,200/- per day and a sum of Rs.19,200/- (1,200 X 16) is awarded under this head.
17. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.
18. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 4 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.66,000/- (16,500 X 4) under this head.
19. MEDICAL EXPENSES :

As per the bills marked at Ex.P13, the petitioner has spent Rs.5,55,860/-
towards medical expenses.
On close perusal of SL.No.13 being the physiotherapy bills.
On perusal of SL.No.17, the bill amount is mentioned as Rs.1559/- but in the said bill it is product name is not mentioned, moreover the bill was issued for what purpose not mentioned.
Hence the said bill amount not considered.

Further on perusal of SL.No.29, 30, 32, 36, 37, 38, 40 are the receipts Jayaprakash M vs Punitha on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69775080/
5 pertaining to physiotherapy.
It is pertinent to note on careful perusal of the said bills, the Court comes to the conclusion that the said bills are created for the purpose of claiming compensation.
Hence they are not considered.
Hence after deduction of the above said bills amount, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,58,301/- which is rounded off to Rs.3,58,300/- towards medical expenses.

20. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '14'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/- p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.2,77,200/- (Rs.16,500 X 12 X 14 X 10/100) is awarded under this head.
21. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Hence a sum of Rs.50,000/- is awarded under this head.
22. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES :
The doctor witness stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
No estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.
But undisputedly petitioner has to undergo surgery for removal of implants, for which he has to necessarily bear certain expenses.
Thus he is entitled to Rs.20,000/- towards future medical and other incidental expenses.

23. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Attendant charges, extra nutritious : 19,200-00 food & conveyance charges 2 Pain &
sufferings : 50,000-00 3 Loss of income during laid-up : 66,000-00 period 4
Medical expenses : 3,58,300-00 5 Loss of future income due to : 2,77,200-00 disability 6 Loss of future amenities & : 50,000-00 happiness 7
Future medical and other : 20,000-00 incidental expenses Total 8,40,700-00 24.

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY: Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
25. It is contended in para 2 of the written statement that, respondent. No.2 has not issued any policy.

Further the respondent No.2 insurance company examined its official as RW.1 and he has produced Ex.R.2 insurance Policy in respect of Yamaha R15 Engine No.G3N4E0538004 and Chasis No.ME1RG67L8P0005132.
However as per the contents of which the issuance of insurance policy is respect of offending vehicle covering the date of accident.
There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is Jayaprakash M vs Punitha on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69775080/
6 primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within two months from the date of this order.
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
26. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.8,40,700/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (Excluding future medical expenses) from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to her through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer and printout taken by him, then corrected and pronounced by me in the open court on this the 4th day of October - 2025)
(Shreyansh Doddamani)
XXI Addl. Small Causes Judge & ACJM, Bengaluru.
